Title: Energy Minimization for Wireless Communication With Rotary-Wing UAV
Authors: Yong Zeng; Jie Xu; Rui Zhang
Prediction target: Instantaneous propulsion power and trajectory energy
Inputs: Forward speed; rotor and airframe parameters
Key result: Derives the widely reused rotary-wing propulsion-power model and optimizes trajectory energy
Major limitation: Steady/idealized flight assumptions; no learned uncertainty
Direct relevance: Supports a transparent instantaneous-power layer and numerical rollout baseline

Title: Energy Model for UAV Communications: Experimental Validation and Model Generalization
Authors: Ning Gao; Yong Zeng; Jian Wang; Di Wu; Chaoyue Zhang; Qingheng Song; Jiachen Qian; Shi Jin
Temporal method: Curve fitting and DNN over flight samples
Key result: Validates the analytical speed-power curve and extends modeling to general 2-D motion
Major limitation: Vehicle- and regime-specific; no mission-risk calibration
Direct relevance: Shows that velocity/acceleration power can be learned before trajectory integration

Title: Energy-Efficient UAV Communications: A Generalized Propulsion Energy Consumption Model
Authors: Xinhong Dai; Bin Duo; Xiaojun Yuan; Wanbin Tang
Prediction target: Instantaneous propulsion power and trajectory energy
Inputs: Velocity; acceleration; flight direction; thrust-to-weight variables
Key result: Generalizes propulsion energy beyond constant-speed straight flight
Major limitation: Requires aerodynamic parameters and modeled dynamics
Direct relevance: Directly motivates using realized velocity and acceleration in TelemetryCostModel

Title: Energy-Efficient UAV Communications in the Presence of Wind: 3D Modeling and Trajectory Design
Authors: Xinhong Dai; Bin Duo; Xiaojun Yuan; Marco Di Renzo
Temporal method: Stochastic-programming trajectory integration with online adaptation
Key result: Extends the generalized propulsion model to stochastic 3-D wind and adaptive trajectories
Major limitation: No real-flight uncertainty calibration
Direct relevance: Shows why future energy-to-go must condition on wind or roll out a wind model

Title: Modeling Power Consumptions for Multirotor UAVs
Authors: Hao Gong; Baoqi Huang; Bing Jia; Hansu Dai
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Inputs: Forward speed; vertical ascent/descent; rotor count and vehicle parameters
Temporal method: Closed-form phase-specific power, combined into 3-D model
Dataset: Real DJI M210 flights and simulation
Key result: Derives forward, ascent, and descent power models and validates them experimentally
Major limitation: Model parameters are platform-specific
Direct relevance: Highlights missing climb/descent physics in the present synthetic cost model

Title: A Comparative Study on Energy Consumption Models for Drones
Authors: Carlos Muli; Sangyoung Park; Mingming Liu
Key result: LSTM outperforms five compared physical models on the studied dataset
Major limitation: Dataset/model transfer is not established; no conservative mission bound
Direct relevance: Supports learning power residuals rather than recursively bootstrapping return quantiles

Title: CVaR-based Flight Energy Risk Assessment for Multirotor UAVs using a Deep Energy Model
Authors: Arnav Choudhry; Brady Moon; Jay Patrikar; Constantine Samaras; Sebastian Scherer
Venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
Prediction target: Trajectory energy distribution and CVaR risk
Inputs: Time-varying flight features; static context; route/weather factors
Temporal method: TCN power prediction followed by Monte Carlo forward simulation
Evaluation metrics: Power prediction error; CVaR flight risk
Key result: Reports 29% better power prediction than an analytical comparator and derives route-level CVaR from forward simulations
Major limitation: Risk quality depends on the learned power and uncertainty models; primarily pre-flight
Direct relevance: Closest architectural precedent for power model + rollout + conservative risk, and a stronger baseline than raw Q95 TD

Title: A Data-Driven Power Consumption Model for Electric UAVs
Authors: Xu Ting Pamela She; Xianke Lin; Haoxiang Lang
Key result: Demonstrates NN power modeling without requiring complete vehicle dynamics
Major limitation: Limited public detail/data and no trajectory-level uncertainty
Direct relevance: Candidate replacement or residual model for real-UAV instantaneous power

Title: Mission-Based Energy Consumption Prediction of Multirotor UAV
Authors: Alex S. Prasetia; Rong-Jong Wai; Yi-Lun Wen; Yu-Kai Wang
Inputs: Mission primitives; GPS; battery log; acceleration/deceleration phases
Temporal method: Movement segmentation plus Elastic Net regression
Key result: Reports 98.773% mean mission-energy accuracy on two surveillance-like test patterns
Major limitation: Small platform/task scope; no uncertainty intervals or online energy-to-go
Direct relevance: Shows direct mission regression can work without Bellman recursion

Title: Vehicle Routing Problems for Drone Delivery
Authors: Kevin Dorling; Jordan Heinrichs; Geoffrey G. Messier; Sebastian Magierowski
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
Inputs: Payload mass; battery mass; maneuver power; route
Temporal method: Segment energy integrated inside routing optimization
Key result: Finds approximately linear dependence on payload and battery weight and embeds it in multi-trip routing
Major limitation: Simplified flight regimes and no online uncertainty
Direct relevance: Shows payload must be context for future transferable energy estimates

Title: Energy Use and Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Emissions of Drones for Commercial Package Delivery
Authors: Joshuah K. Stolaroff; Constantine Samaras; Emma R. O'Neill; Alia Lubers; Alexandra S. Mitchell; Daniel Ceperley
Dataset: Real flight measurements plus scenario simulation
Key result: Quantifies how package mass, range, and warehousing affect delivery energy and emissions
Major limitation: Not an online control estimator
Direct relevance: Provides real-flight evidence that distance alone is insufficient across payload/context

Title: Drone Flight Data Reveal Energy and Greenhouse Gas Emissions Savings for Very Small Package Delivery
Authors: Thiago A. Rodrigues; Jay Patrikar; Natalia L. Oliveira; H. Scott Matthews; Sebastian Scherer; Constantine Samaras
Inputs: Position; speed; acceleration; wind; payload; measured voltage/current
Temporal method: Power regression integrated over delivery flight
Key result: Produces a simple empirical model for similar small drones below 12 m/s using real delivery-flight data
Major limitation: Limited platform/speed envelope
Direct relevance: Strong real-flight dataset candidate for later calibration of the instantaneous layer

Title: Energy-Aware Coverage Path Planning of UAVs
Authors: Carmelo Di Franco; Giorgio Buttazzo
Key result: Optimizes coverage speed/path using an energy model rather than Euclidean distance alone
Major limitation: Known coverage paths; no online distributional uncertainty
Direct relevance: Baseline evidence for trajectory rollout/integration

Title: Energy-Aware Spiral Coverage Path Planning for UAV Photogrammetric Applications
Authors: Taua M. Cabreira; Carmelo Di Franco; Paulo R. Ferreira; Giorgio C. Buttazzo
Inputs: Polygon geometry; altitude; camera overlap; segment speed
Temporal method: Path-specific speed optimization and energy integration
Dataset: Over 3,500 simulated areas and real flights
Evaluation metrics: Time and energy savings; prediction precision
Key result: Real flights report 7.7% energy improvement and the revised model improves energy-estimation precision by 13.41%
Major limitation: Specialized photogrammetry paths
Direct relevance: Demonstrates model-based trajectory energy can be both interpretable and accurate

Title: Autonomous Recharging and Flight Mission Planning for Battery-Operated Autonomous Drones
Authors: Rashid Alyassi; Majid Khonji; Areg Karapetyan; Sid Chi-Kin Chau; Khaled Elbassioni; Chien-Ming Tseng
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
Temporal method: Learned expenditure model embedded in asymmetric TSP planning
Key result: Jointly plans flight and recharging with a learned energy model and approximation guarantees
Major limitation: Planning assumes model estimates are adequate; no online calibrated tail bound
Direct relevance: Closest charging-planning comparator; uses model+planning rather than TD return quantiles

Title: Energy-Aware Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ground-to-Air Charging
Authors: Bill Cai; Fei Lu; Lifeng Zhou
Inputs: UAV/UGV energy budgets; guided tour; charging opportunities
Temporal method: TSP guide plus Monte Carlo Tree Search
Uncertainty method: Search uncertainty, not calibrated energy risk
Key result: Uses MCTS to refine energy-constrained routes with a mobile charger
Major limitation: Energy model and uncertainty treatment are application-specific
Direct relevance: Relevant planning baseline for charging but not a learned energy-to-go estimator

Title: AutoCharge: Autonomous Charging for Perpetual Quadrotor Missions
Authors: Alessandro Saviolo; Jeffrey Mao; Roshan Balu T M B; Vivek Radhakrishnan; Giuseppe Loianno
Venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
Inputs: Relative docking pose; charging hardware state
Key result: Demonstrates a 10-hour perpetual quadrotor mission with repeated charge cycles
Major limitation: Does not estimate mission energy or switching risk
Direct relevance: Clarifies that recharge continuity is a systems problem separate from energy-to-go prediction

Title: Delivery by Drones with Arbitrary Energy Consumption Models: A New Formulation Approach
Authors: Amir Ahmadi-Javid; Mahla Meskar
Inputs: Arbitrary segment energy function; payload; hovering/time windows
Temporal method: Linearized routing formulation over supplied energy model
Dataset: 255 benchmark instances and larger synthetic instances
Key result: Allows nonconvex energy functions without approximating the energy model inside routing
Major limitation: Does not learn or calibrate the supplied energy model
Direct relevance: Shows downstream planning can remain agnostic to whether energy comes from physics, rollout, or learning

Title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences
Authors: Richard S. Sutton
Key result: Introduces TD prediction as bootstrapping between Monte Carlo and dynamic programming
Major limitation: Classical/tabular or linear setting; not neural SSP distributional stability
Direct relevance: Defines the bootstrap mechanism under diagnosis

Title: An Analysis of Temporal-Difference Learning with Function Approximation
Authors: John N. Tsitsiklis; Benjamin Van Roy
Key result: Gives convergence and approximation results under stated linear/on-policy conditions
Major limitation: Does not justify arbitrary nonlinear gamma=1 TD
Direct relevance: Supports caution against extrapolating tabular/linear convergence to the current critic

Title: Fast Gradient-Descent Methods for Temporal-Difference Learning with Linear Function Approximation
Authors: Richard S. Sutton; Hamid Reza Maei; Doina Precup; Shalabh Bhatnagar; David Silver; Csaba Szepesvari; Eric Wiewiora
Key result: Provides true stochastic-gradient TD algorithms with off-policy linear convergence properties
Major limitation: Linear approximation and extra auxiliary weights; not directly neural quantile TD
Direct relevance: Candidate if bootstrapped policy evaluation remains necessary

Title: A Distributional Perspective on Reinforcement Learning
Authors: Marc G. Bellemare; Will Dabney; Remi Munos
Key result: Establishes distributional Bellman structure and exposes instability distinctions between evaluation and control
Major limitation: Discounted bounded-return categorical setting; not four sparse SSP quantiles
Direct relevance: Shows projection choice is part of the algorithm, not an interchangeable detail

Title: Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Quantile Regression
Authors: Will Dabney; Mark Rowland; Marc G. Bellemare; Remi Munos
Prediction target: Full return distribution through quantile locations
Uncertainty method: Uniform equal-probability atoms at quantile midpoints
Key result: Derives a Wasserstein-consistent distributional projection with fixed uniform probabilities and adjustable locations
Major limitation: Discounted Atari control; theory does not cover arbitrary nonuniform sparse masses
Direct relevance: Directly contradicts treating the current four custom-weighted quantiles as standard QR-DQN

Title: Implicit Quantile Networks for Distributional Reinforcement Learning
Authors: Will Dabney; Georg Ostrovski; David Silver; Remi Munos
Uncertainty method: Sampled quantile fractions and distortion risk measures
Key result: Learns the full quantile function rather than four fixed tail landmarks
Major limitation: Still bootstrapped and evaluated in discounted control; more complex than needed here
Direct relevance: A principled alternative if a true return distribution is later necessary

Title: An Analysis of Categorical Distributional Reinforcement Learning
Authors: Mark Rowland; Marc Bellemare; Will Dabney; Remi Munos; Yee Whye Teh
Key result: Formalizes that convergence is tied to the chosen projected operator and metric
Major limitation: Categorical/tabular focus, not nonlinear quantile SSP
Direct relevance: Supports diagnosing the custom projection rather than blaming gamma alone

Title: Safe and Efficient Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning
Authors: Remi Munos; Tom Stepleton; Anna Harutyunyan; Marc G. Bellemare
Key result: Derives a contractive multi-step operator with variance/off-policy corrections
Major limitation: Designed for discounted control, not deterministic gamma=1 energy evaluation
Direct relevance: Supports testing multi-step targets to reduce one-step recursive dependence

Title: True Online TD(lambda)
Authors: Harm van Seijen; Richard S. Sutton
Key result: Makes online TD(lambda) exactly match a revised forward view at the same asymptotic cost
Major limitation: Primarily linear expected-value prediction
Direct relevance: Principled alternative to an ad hoc fixed n-step target

Title: Why Target Networks Stabilise Temporal Difference Methods
Authors: Mattie Fellows; Matthew J. A. Smith; Shimon Whiteson
Temporal method: Partially fitted policy evaluation with target networks
Key result: Shows target networks mitigate conditioning only under regularity and a suitably tuned update frequency
Major limitation: Does not imply every nonlinear distributional TD is stable
Direct relevance: Explains why changing tau can alter drift but cannot repair a wrong projection

Title: Target Network and Truncation Overcome the Deadly Triad in Q-Learning
Authors: Zaiwei Chen; John-Paul Clarke; Siva Theja Maguluri
Venue: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
Key result: Establishes stability under explicit target-network and truncation conditions
Major limitation: Requires algorithmic truncation/assumptions absent from current code
Direct relevance: Shows a target network alone is not a general divergence guarantee

Title: The Pitfalls of Regularization in Off-Policy TD Learning
Authors: Gaurav Manek; J. Zico Kolter
Key result: Shows common regularization does not generally eliminate TD instability, including neural examples
Major limitation: Focuses off-policy deadly-triad settings; our data are nearly on-policy
Direct relevance: Rules out proposing weight decay or smaller norms as a sufficient remedy

Title: Target Networks and Over-parameterization Stabilize Off-policy Bootstrapping with Function Approximation
Authors: Fengdi Che; Chenjun Xiao; Jincheng Mei; Bo Dai; Ramki Gummadi; Oscar A. Ramirez; Christopher K. Harris; A. Rupam Mahmood; Dale Schuurmans
Key result: Proves weaker convergence conditions for a specific overparameterized linear setting
Major limitation: Does not cover the current nonlinear monotone quantile projection
Direct relevance: Further limits what can be inferred from merely having a target network

Title: Batch Policy Learning under Constraints
Authors: Hoang Le; Cameron Voloshin; Yisong Yue
Key result: Provides a practical fitted policy-evaluation subroutine with finite-sample analysis
Major limitation: Discounted batch setting and policy-level values, not online SSP tails
Direct relevance: Relevant scalar fitted-evaluation baseline and warning about approximation/distribution shift

Title: Bootstrapping Fitted Q-Evaluation for Off-Policy Inference
Authors: Botao Hao; Xiang Ji; Yaqi Duan; Hao Lu; Csaba Szepesvari; Mengdi Wang
Key result: Derives efficient distributionally consistent inference for FQE error in tabular/linear regimes
Major limitation: Statistical bootstrap is distinct from Bellman bootstrapping and assumptions are limited
Direct relevance: Useful distinction between calibrated estimator uncertainty and raw return quantiles

Title: Off-Policy Fitted Q-Evaluation with Differentiable Function Approximators: Z-Estimation and Inference Theory
Authors: Ruiqi Zhang; Xuezhou Zhang; Chengzhuo Ni; Mengdi Wang
Key result: Connects FQE error to tangent space, reward, and distribution shift for differentiable approximators
Major limitation: Still requires regularity/coverage and targets mean value
Direct relevance: Supports separating point estimation from statistically justified uncertainty
